question: Using Logisim Evolution, design a BCD-to-seven-segment display circuit using the 7447-decoder IC. Connect the decoder outputs to a seven-segment display and test all 16 possible 4-bit input combinations. Record the segment pattern displayed for each input and identify which codes correspond to valid BCD digits (0-9) and which correspond to invalid BCD codes (10-15). Caution: The 7447 decoder has active-low segment outputs; therefore, a logic 0 turns a segment ON, while a logic 1 turns it OFF. Account for this active-low operation while wiring the circuit and interpreting the segment patterns

source.file: lab manual, Experiment 9.7 open ended question (screenshot)

design_notes.choice: the 7447 from Logisim Evolution's TTL library, as the question requires
design_notes.rationale: the question names the part; a gate-level equivalent would answer a different question, and the 7447's own decode of the six invalid codes is part of what is being observed

design_notes.choice: LT, BI and RBI are tied to one input pin EN, which must be held HIGH to read the BCD decode
design_notes.rationale: all three are active low. Evolution's 7447 leaves them as real ports, and a floating control pin would make every segment output undefined, so they are driven from a single pin the student can see and set rather than left dangling

design_notes.choice: each segment drives BOTH an output pin and the display
design_notes.rationale: the display is what the question asks to observe, but a display has no outputs and cannot appear in a truth table. The output pins are what makes the segment pattern recordable for all sixteen codes

asks.text: Record the segment pattern displayed for each input
